correctness.rationale: For distinct nonzero zero divisors, multiplication vanishes exactly when the valuations sum to at least m. In the kernel equations the deleted diagonal forces constancy on every high layer. Only the socle high layer has size nonzero modulo p; the V_1 equation forces its constant to vanish, and the socle equation then forces the total of the low coordinates to vanish. Each remaining high layer is uniquely determined by the specified tail of low sums. This gives the stated rank and makes the kernel pairing the ordinary dot product on a low-coordinate zero-sum hyperplane. Its radical is the all-ones line, because the low layer sizes are multiples of p, and this vector has zero high extension. No vertex is isolated, so the dual has no unit vector; two low vertices in one layer give a weight-two dual word. The primal distance-one witness follows from r_b-r_a=e_a-e_b for socle vertices and r_u=1_socle for u in V_1, with q-1 invertible in the coefficient field, including the singleton socle. Independently constructed the graphs using actual ring multiplication in Z/81, F_3[x]/(x^4) and F_2[x]/(x^5); ranks were 9, 9, 4 and hull dimensions were 1 via rank(A)-rank(A^2). The length-five case tested a nonzero high-coordinate lift. Replay: python3 /workspace/review_evidence/4-check.py. These instances confirm rather than prove the general argument.
residual_risks: The direct-ring reproduction checks only three specified rings; extension residue fields and arbitrary lengths are covered by the proof, not by that reproduction.
